findings.evidence: ApproximatesToOrder.lean lines 54-77 define `refl`, `mono`, `congr`, `trans` and nothing else; `grep -n approximatesToOrder_iff` shows the escape-hatch used at Matching.lean:256,257 and PowerCorrections.lean:120,122.
findings.fix: Add `lemma ApproximatesToOrder.symm {W Wapp n} (h : ApproximatesToOrder W Wapp n) : ApproximatesToOrder Wapp W n` and rewrite both call sites as `h₁.symm.trans h₂` followed by `.congr`, so consumers never need `approximatesToOrder_iff` to compare two approximants.
findings.issue: The module advertises the relation as "reflexive and transitive" and supplies `ApproximatesToOrder.refl`/`.trans`/`.mono`/`.congr`, but not `.symm`, which holds trivially (`IsBigO.neg_left` on the difference). Consequence: the PR's own proofs cannot express "two approximations of the same function differ by `O(λ^n)`" inside the API and drop to raw `IsBigO`: `Matching.lean:256-257` (`(approximatesToOrder_iff.1 (hc a)).sub (approximatesToOrder_iff.1 (hc' a))`) and `PowerCorrections.lean:119-127` (`h₁'.sub h₂'` after two `approximatesToOrder_iff.1` unfoldings).

findings.evidence: upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/Data/Fintype/Card.lean:365-366 — `@[simp] theorem Fintype.card_coe (s : Finset α) [Fintype s] : Fintype.card s = #s`.
findings.fix: State the condition as `(P.matchingMatrix M k).rank = (P.totalDegreePiece k).card` in `IsMatching.eqOn_totalDegreePiece` (272), `eqOn_truncation` (283), `forall_eqOn_totalDegreePiece_iff` (295) and `forall_eqOn_truncation_iff` (329), inserting `Fintype.card_coe` internally where TauCeti's `Matrix.rank_eq_card_iff_mulVec_injective` is applied.
findings.issue: The rank hypothesis is stated as `(P.matchingMatrix M k).rank = Fintype.card (P.totalDegreePiece k)`, i.e. `Fintype.card ↥(Finset …)`. `Fintype.card_coe` is `@[simp]` in Mathlib, so this is not simp-normal: a consumer who `simp`s the hypothesis or the goal gets `#(P.totalDegreePiece k)` and no longer matches the lemma. This affects all four uniqueness statements that carry the condition.

findings.evidence: ApproximatesToOrder.lean:8 is the file's only import; the sole use of TruncatedExpansion is `isBigO_pow_pow` at line 62, inside a proof term.
findings.fix: Demote to `import EpsilonEridani.Mathematics.Analysis.Asymptotics.TruncatedExpansion` and add `public import Mathlib.Analysis.Asymptotics.Lemmas` directly. Matching.lean:11 and PowerCorrections.lean:10 already carry their own private `import` of TruncatedExpansion, so nothing downstream breaks.
findings.issue: `public import …Asymptotics.TruncatedExpansion` re-exports that module to every downstream consumer, but no statement in this file mentions anything from it — it is used only in the proof of `ApproximatesToOrder.mono` (`isBigO_pow_pow`). The file's public statements need Mathlib's `Asymptotics`/`Topology`, which it currently gets only transitively.

summary: The surface is mostly well-formed (bodies unexposed, `*_def`/`mem_*` lemmas present, no compatibility residue), but `ApproximatesToOrder` ships `refl`/`trans` without `symm`, which its own consumers need and therefore bypass into raw `IsBigO`; the central rank hypothesis is stated in a non-simp-normal form; and one `public import` over-exposes a proof-only dependency.
